public_rationale: Marcus states this as his own belief ('I believe') about how 'all too often' employers misjudge what humans and AI can do. He names no measure, threshold, or period. Whether employers underestimate humans or overestimate AI is a judgment about their beliefs, and no public data could confirm or refute how often it happens. Cases like Klarna, whose CEO said its AI-first approach 'wasn't the right path', fit his view. But single examples cannot test a hedged frequency claim, so I don't score it.
limitations: Reviewers who read it as a factual claim might score it from examples like Klarna. I judged the hedging too strong for that.
